newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit eases on fresh overseas sales, Thai woes.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit eases on fresh overseas sales, Thai woes.

text.p: * Ringgit resumes fall on fresh selling by U.S. funds
* Thai economic woes remain cause for fresh dumping in regional currencies
* Dollar/ringgit could test 2.6550 again in thin trading
The ringgit resumed its fall overnight on sales by U.S. funds on fresh worries about Thailand's economic problems, dealers said on Thursday.
Dealers said strong bids for dollar/Sing was also causing an easing of the ringgit.
"Dollar/Sing is looking very biddish. That is also pulling up dollar/Malay," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
He said hedge funds, which were yesterday taking profit in dollar/ringgit, had done an about turn and were again dumping the ringgit. There was strong demand for dollar at 2.6250.

"Now with Thailand seeking funds from IMF and having to obey fresh international conditions with regards to its economy, there is fresh excuse of regional instability for the punters," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
He said until Thailand settled down, the turmoil in regional currencies was expected to continue.
The dealer said Wednesday's profit-taking was done in very small volumes.
At 0250 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6370/80 to a dollar.
